claims.text: xUnit discovers test methods marked [Fact] in public classes of the test project and runs each one; no separate registration list is needed.
claims.source_hint: xUnit docs: getting started (Fact), test discovery; xUnit analyzer xUnit1000 (test classes must be public)

claims.text: A [Fact] method must not take parameters; it returns void, or Task for an async test.
claims.source_hint: xUnit docs: Fact vs Theory (Fact takes no data), async tests returning Task; analyzer xUnit1001

claims.text: Assert.Equal's first parameter is the expected value and the second the actual value; a failure message labels them Expected and Actual.
claims.source_hint: xUnit Assert.Equal<T>(T expected, T actual); xunit 2.9.2 failure message format

claims.text: OrderEncapsulatedTests.TotalFollowsTheLines adds lines 1×1,250,000 and 2×450,000 and asserts Assert.Equal(2_150_000, order.TotalVnd); AnEmptyOrderCannotBePaid asserts Assert.Throws<InvalidOperationException>(order.MarkPaid).
OrderEncapsulated.MarkPaid throws InvalidOperationException when the order has no lines.
Assert.Throws<T>(Action) invokes the delegate and passes only if an exception of exactly type T is thrown (not a derived type).
claims.source_hint: xUnit Assert.Throws<T> docs (exact type; ThrowsAny for derived)

claims.text: Adding the ExpressShippingAlwaysCostsSixtyThousand test to ShippingFeeTests makes the filtered run report three passed; with expected 50_000 it fails with Expected 50000 and Actual 60000; with the arguments swapped the labels swap.
claims.source_hint: follows from claims 1, 3, 7; SamplesTests.cs:7-25 (two existing ShippingFeeTests)
